questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Loosely.
Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Hidden beneath the seat.
So the buzzer or light stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should fit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off all lights.
Use only your parking lights.
Use only your headlights.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights on. Make sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: When can you safely pass on a two-lane, two-way street?

options.text: When you can clearly see the road ahead.
When you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
When your vehicle has enough speed to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass safely on a two-lane street unless you can clearly see the road ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Both directions can pass.
No passing is allowed.
You can pass at the top of a hill.
You can pass during daylight.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic on the other side is going the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: What should you do when you see railroad tracks ahead?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate comes down.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Don't worry about how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains or vehicles using the tracks. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When can you legally pass another vehicle on the right side?

options.text: If the vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you have to drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right when there is a passing lane and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on multilane roads with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what the other cars are doing, even if it goes against the guard's directions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be cautious when a sign, crossing guard, or officer tells you to. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red signals and gates are present and working.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, a stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are working.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Stay farther back from the car ahead.
Don't drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: At night, you can't see as well. Take steps to make night driving safer for you and other drivers.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When driving through an intersection.
When passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when they don't see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely. This helps you avoid road rage and dangerous situations.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be unsafe. If you are on a two-lane road and traffic is backing up behind you, you must pull over and let cars pass. Only drive slowly when road conditions require it.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Sound your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers right away. Move as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car is disabled.

questions.question: When can you drive across a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross these lines to change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to frighten them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always give way to pedestrians, even if you have a green light. Pedestrian safety comes first. Be careful around pedestrians in every situation.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, pull safely to the right side of the road and stop. Make room for the emergency vehicle to pass. If you are in heavy traffic, slow down and move over as soon as you can.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must or must not do. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your turn signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your rearview mirror, side mirror, and look over your shoulder. Always signal before you change lanes. These steps help you stay safe.

questions.question: What colors are signs that show the distance to the next exit on a highway?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Information signs about destinations are green with white letters.

questions.question: A driver under 21 with a probationary license:

options.text: May use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
May not drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
Should not wear a seat belt while driving.
May use a hand-held cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
questions.explanation: Drivers with probationary licenses have restrictions. They cannot use any cell phone while driving and must wear a seat belt. Drivers under 21 cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up as they pass you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If you encounter an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact with them. Do not speed up, as this may make them angrier and increase danger.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a last-minute turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, go to the next one instead.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can be dangerous to infants and small children, even in low-speed crashes.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before you drive, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children 12 and under should ride restrained in a rear seat. Never put a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a front passenger airbag.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to reduce your risk of being injured or killed in a traffic crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to hours between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective thing you can do to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Call the police immediately.
Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Flash your vehicle's lights to let them know they are wrong.
Use a driving action to get back at the aggressive driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get even with an aggressive driver can make the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving ability?

options.text: The same way alcohol does.
The same way amphetamines do.
The same way anger does.
The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol does.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving ability. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving as much as a 0.05 percent blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours impairs your driving as much as a 0.10 percent blood alcohol level.

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the roadway, what should you do?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, go to the next one or find a safe place to turn around. Do not back up.

questions.question: In what ways can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It gives you false confidence.
It impairs your thinking ability.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, impairs your coordination and balance, and affects your vision and ability to judge distance.
